corrections.why: Harriman State Park is where the tower stood. Wikipedia and WillhiteWeb name the Palisades State Park Commission as the body that built it.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A December 1927 newspaper item, quoted by the Eastern site, says one tower was being built on the northeast summit; Wikipedia and WillhiteWeb date the 60-foot steel tower to 1928. The story reports both.

Wikipedia says the tower was closed and removed in the early 1970s. WillhiteWeb says it stood closed through the 1970s and into the early 1980s and was taken apart by the mid-1980s. The story reports both and does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: The 1928 build, the 60-foot Aermotor LS40 height (18 m) and the three-tower plan are consistent across Wikipedia, WillhiteWeb and the Eastern site. The 1915 wooden pole tower and the late-1960s seasonal staffing rest on WillhiteWeb alone. The removal date conflicts (early 1970s vs mid-1980s) are unresolved. Eastern site gives only 'Removed' with no date. The 'Harriman State Park' agency value in the record is corrected to the Palisades State Park Commission. WillhiteWeb photo captions (a 1928 steel tower photo credited to Larry Paul; a 1915 pole tower; the lookout site) show what the site looked like, but no image URLs were retrieved, so no photos are listed. A 1927 New York Times archive item appeared in search results but could not be read through the cache, so it is not used. A Facebook group post in search results mentions a Harriman tower removed in the late 1950s or early 1960s over vandalism; it does not say which tower, so it is not used.
